Definition: to be straight or even; figuratively, to be (causatively, to make) right, pleasant, prosperous
BiblicalUsage: Yâshar is the verb for making straight, for directing a path so it does not bend. Solomon promises that if I acknowledge God in all my ways, He shall direct my paths, and the kine carrying the ark took the straight way to Beth-shemesh and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left. The righteousness of the perfect directs his way, and what pleases God is the thing that is right in the eyes of His people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God directs the paths of those who acknowledge Him, and the straight way is the way He Himself marks. My position is that a directed life is not a restricted life but a delivered one, because the straight road reaches home. And I hold that the ark found its own way to Beth-shemesh, and God will direct me too if I do not turn aside.
